extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: FLORES-101 is an evaluation benchmark for low-resource and multilingual machine translation consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: en, afr, amh, ara, hye, asm, ast, azj, bel, ben, bos, bul, mya, cat, ceb, zho, hrv, ces, dan, nld, est, tgl, fin, fra, ful, glg, lug, kat, deu, ell, guj, hau, heb, hin, hun, isl, ibo, ind, gle, ita
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involved extracting sentences from English Wikipedia sources (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage) by randomly selecting articles and manually choosing 3 to 5 contiguous sentences per article. These sentences were then professionally translated into 101 languages through a controlled workflow involving translation Language Service Providers (LSPs), automatic checks, and human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of English sentences extracted from three Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (international news), Wikijunior (children's nonfiction books), and WikiVoyage (travel guides), covering a broad range of topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were manually labeled with sub-topics by in-house annotators. For the translation task, sentences were translated by a Language Service Provider (LSP), automatically checked, and then evaluated by a second LSP with a feedback loop for re-translation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translations were validated through a multi-step quality control process involving automatic checks and human evaluation by a secondary Language Service Provider, with multiple rounds of evaluation if necessary.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female) working as researchers and program/project managers, originating from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to positively impact the majority of the global population who speak low-resource languages by enabling improvements in machine translation quality for their native languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to be used as an evaluation benchmark for assessing machine translation model quality, specifically for low-resource languages and many-to-many multilingual translation systems.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was balanced across three domains (Wikinews, Wikijunior, WikiVoyage) and sampled equally from different locations within the articles (beginning, middle, end) to avoid document structure bias.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was filtered by manually selecting contiguous sentences and removing segments that were too short or malformed.

isLiveDataset.evidence: consisting of 3001 sentences sampled from English Wikipedia and professionally translated in 101 languages.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article... These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources... we opted to source all sentences from English Wikipedia

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we collected a third of the sentences from Wikinews, which is a collection of international news articles, a third from Wikijunior, which is a collection of age-appropriate nonfiction books for children from birth to age 12, and a third from WikiVoyage which is a travel guide with a collection of articles about travel tips, food and destinations around the globe.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We manually labeled all sentences by a more detailed sub-topic... For each target language, sentences are translated by a translation Language Service Provider (LSP). The resulting translations are automatically checked. If these checks fail, translations are sent back for re-translation. If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation. If the quality is not sufficient, translations are sent back to the original translation LSP for re-translation. Depending on the human score, the process can repeat for multiple rounds of human evaluation.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: The selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in our lab, 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research: researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; originally coming from different regions of the world: East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Yet, the majority of the world’s population speak low-resource languages and would beneﬁt from improvements in translation quality on their native languages.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The resulting dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages, including the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems, as all translations are multilingually aligned.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We balanced the location selection to be equally distributed across the whole corpus — roughly one third of paragraphs were sampled from the beginning of the article, one third from the middle, and so on.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences.
